hook.text: A nano sensor stuck to a leaf measures plant stress hormones — precision farming at the molecular level.

buildup.text: Carbon nanotube sensors detect ethylene, the ripening hormone, at sub-ppm levels from intact plants.

discovery.text: Early stress detection lets farmers intervene before crop damage is visible — saving yields and reducing waste.

twist.text: Outdoor conditions — UV, rain, dust — degrade sensor coatings within weeks, limiting field deployment.

climax.text: Encapsulated nano sensors on biodegradable substrates decompose after harvest — no plastic waste left behind.

punchline.text: A nano patch on a leaf reports stress before the farmer can see it.

quiz.question: How do nanosensors help precision agriculture?
options: They detect plant stress hormones early, allowing intervention before visible crop damage
They increase the growth rate of plants
